mnemonic.meaning: 切 is cut: you cut things off at some point. An end, a limit, a stopping point.
mnemonic.reading: KEY, REE (きり): you cut the key ring, and that's the end of it. No more keys.

examples.ja: 切りがいいところで休みましょう。
examples.en: Let's take a break at a good stopping point.

items.note: 切りがない = there's no end to it. Often written in kana: きりがない.

mnemonic.meaning: "IT'S MADE MO' (いつまでも) delicious every time," grandma says. She'll keep cooking it forever, endlessly.

examples.ja: いつまでも元気でいてください。
examples.en: Please stay healthy forever.

items.note: Warm and common in wishes. ずっと is close but more neutral.

mnemonic.meaning: "NOW, OH (なお)... and in addition," the speaker adds one more thing. Still more, further.

examples.ja: なお、詳しいことは後日お知らせします。
examples.en: In addition, we will announce the details at a later date.

items.note: In notices, なお = "please note". As an adverb, なお + adjective = even more: なおいい.

mnemonic.meaning: The only (唯) one (一). There's no other: the sole, unique one.
mnemonic.reading: "YOU, EAT SUE's (ゆいいつ) cake?" It was the only one left!

examples.ja: 彼は私の唯一の友達だ。
examples.en: He is my only friend.

items.note: Used as 唯一の + noun. ただ一つの and たった一人の are softer alternatives.

mnemonic.meaning: 差 has 工 (craft) under a twisted roof: two craftsmen's work side by side shows the gap. A difference.
mnemonic.reading: SAW (さ): the saw cuts two planks, and you measure the difference between them.

examples.ja: 二人の実力には大きな差がある。
examples.en: There is a big gap in ability between the two.

items.note: 差がつく = a gap opens up. 差がない = no difference.

mnemonic.meaning: MAT, TOE, MEh-RUE (まとめる): you gather everything onto one mat with your toe and put it all together. To summarize the mess.

examples.ja: 会議の内容を一枚にまとめた。
examples.en: I summarized the meeting on one page.

items.note: Intransitive form: まとまる (to come together). まとめて = all at once.

mnemonic.meaning: Since (以) you came (来), everything changed. Ever since.
mnemonic.reading: EAR, EYE (いらい): ever since the accident, your ear and eye have hurt.

examples.ja: 卒業して以来、彼に会っていない。
examples.en: I haven't seen him since we graduated.

items.note: Comes after V-て or a noun: 去年以来 (since last year). Don't confuse with 依頼 (いらい, request), Level 5.

mnemonic.meaning: 至 is an arrow landing on the ground: it has reached its extreme point. To reach, to lead to.
mnemonic.reading: EAT A ROO (いたる)? The road finally reaches the outback, where they serve kangaroo.

examples.ja: 長い話し合いの結果、結論に至った。
examples.en: After a long discussion, we arrived at a conclusion.

items.note: Formal. 至るところ = everywhere. 〜に至るまで = all the way down to.

mnemonic.meaning: Not (不) full (満): you're not satisfied. Dissatisfaction, a complaint.
mnemonic.reading: "FOO, MAN (ふまん)!" you grumble at the tiny portion. Dissatisfaction.

examples.ja: 社員たちは給料に不満を持っている。
examples.en: The employees are dissatisfied with their pay.

items.note: 不満を言う = to complain. 満足 (まんぞく) is the opposite.

mnemonic.meaning: The whole (全) body (体), every part of it. The whole, overall.
mnemonic.reading: ZEN TIE (ぜんたい): the monk ties his whole body in a knot. The entire thing.

examples.ja: クラス全体で話し合った。
examples.en: We talked it over as a whole class.

items.note: 全体的に = overall. 全部 is "all of it", 全体 is "the whole thing as one".

mnemonic.meaning: 含 has 口 (mouth) under 今 (now): you hold something in your mouth. You include it.
mnemonic.reading: FOOK, MEh-RUE (ふくめる): the waiter includes the tip in the bill. Fook, you regret ordering.

examples.ja: 税金を含めて千円です。
examples.en: It's 1,000 yen including tax.

items.note: 含める = to include something (you do it). 含む (ふくむ) = to contain (it already does).

mnemonic.meaning: "SO, NO OOCHIE (そのうち)... yet," says the kid on a skateboard. One of these days, eventually.

examples.ja: そのうち雨もやむでしょう。
examples.en: The rain will stop before long.

items.note: Vague future: "sometime soon". そのうちに is the same.

mnemonic.meaning: "EE-WAH, YOU RULE (いわゆる)!" shouts the so-called "king" of the playground. What they call a king.

examples.ja: 彼はいわゆる天才だ。
examples.en: He is what people call a genius.

items.note: Comes right before a noun. Used to introduce a common term, often a little ironic.

mnemonic.meaning: Stand (立ち) and go up (上がる). You stand up, get up, rise up.
mnemonic.reading: TACHI, AH, GARUUU (たちあがる)! You groan like a monster as you stand up from the couch.

examples.ja: 彼は椅子から立ち上がった。
examples.en: He stood up from his chair.

items.note: Also figurative: rise up against something, or a computer starting up.

mnemonic.meaning: YA, GATE (やがて): before long, the yak reaches the gate. Soon, eventually.

examples.ja: やがて雨が止んで、空が明るくなった。
examples.en: Before long the rain stopped and the sky got brighter.

items.note: Written and story-like. Narrates something that happens after a while.

mnemonic.meaning: FOOT, OH (ふと)! Suddenly, unexpectedly, you stub your foot.

examples.ja: ふと昔のことを思い出した。
examples.en: I suddenly remembered the old days.

items.note: For thoughts or actions that happen without planning: ふと思う, ふと見る. Not for loud sudden events (that's 突然).

mnemonic.meaning: SO TOE (そっと): you walk on your toes, softly, gently, quietly.

examples.ja: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、そっとドアを閉めた。
examples.en: The baby was sleeping, so I closed the door quietly.

items.note: そっとしておく = leave someone alone.

mnemonic.meaning: GEE, TOE (じっと)! Keep still, the doctor says, holding your toe. Motionless.

examples.ja: 猫が窓の外をじっと見ている。
examples.en: The cat is staring out of the window.

items.note: じっと見る = to stare. じっとする = to keep still.

mnemonic.meaning: 肌 has 月 (flesh) on the left: the outer layer of your flesh. Your skin.
mnemonic.reading: HA-DA (はだ): "HA, DA sun burned my skin!"

examples.ja: 冬は肌が乾燥しやすい。
examples.en: Skin gets dry easily in winter.

items.note: 皮膚 (ひふ) is the medical word. 肌 is everyday, also for texture and feel.

mnemonic.meaning: 頬 has 頁 (head): the side of your face. Your cheek.
mnemonic.reading: "HO HO (ほほ)!" laughs Santa, cheeks rosy.

examples.ja: 恥ずかしくて頬が赤くなった。
examples.en: My cheeks turned red with embarrassment.

items.note: Both ほほ and ほお are correct.

mnemonic.meaning: "ARE YOU HA... (あるいは)" happy, or possibly sad? Or perhaps both.

examples.ja: 電話、あるいはメールで連絡してください。
examples.en: Please contact us by phone or email.

items.note: Formal version of または / か. Also "perhaps": あるいは本当かもしれない.

mnemonic.meaning: 互 is two hooks linked: each hooks the other. Mutual, each other.
mnemonic.reading: OH, TAG, GUY (おたがい)! Two guys tag each other back and forth.

examples.ja: お互いに助け合いましょう。
examples.en: Let's help each other.

items.note: お互い様 = "we're in the same boat", said when both sides owe each other.

mnemonic.meaning: One (一) word (言). Just a few words.
mnemonic.reading: HE TOE-COTO (ひとこと): he says just one word, then stubs his toe.

examples.ja: 最後に一言お願いします。
examples.en: Please say a few words to finish.

items.note: Note the reading: ひとこと, not いちげん.

mnemonic.meaning: 酒 has 氵 (liquid) + 酉 (jar): liquid in a jar. Alcohol.
mnemonic.reading: SAKE (さけ): the Japanese rice wine you already know.

examples.ja: 父は毎晩少し酒を飲む。
examples.en: My father drinks a little alcohol every night.

items.note: In Japan 酒 means any alcohol; rice wine specifically is 日本酒.

mnemonic.meaning: Not (ない) differing (違い) from the truth: it must be so. No doubt.
mnemonic.reading: CHEE, GUY, NIGH (ちがいない): "The cheese guy is nigh, no doubt, I smell him."

examples.ja: 彼はもう家に帰ったに違いない。
examples.en: He must have gone home already.

items.note: Used as 〜に違いない. Strong certainty.

mnemonic.meaning: Fly (飛び) out (出す). You jump out, rush out.
mnemonic.reading: TOE, BEAD, DOSS (とびだす): a bead pops off your toe and jumps out the door.

examples.ja: 子供が道路に飛び出した。
examples.en: A child ran out into the road.

items.note: Also "to stick out" or "to leave suddenly": 家を飛び出す.

mnemonic.meaning: Many (多) or few (少): more or less. Somewhat.
mnemonic.reading: TASH, SHOW (たしょう): your moustache shows a little, more or less.

examples.ja: 多少高くても、質のいい物を買いたい。
examples.en: I want to buy good-quality things, even if they're a bit expensive.

items.note: A bit formal; 少し is everyday. 多少の = some, a certain amount of.

accept: together with others of the same kind

mnemonic.meaning: Samurai (士) of the same (同) clan. Fellows, companions.
mnemonic.reading: DOUGH SHE (どうし) shares with her fellow bakers. Companions.

examples.ja: 友達同士で旅行に行った。
examples.en: We went on a trip together, as a group of friends.

items.note: Usually after a noun: 恋人同士 (a couple), 日本人同士 (between Japanese people).

mnemonic.meaning: 悔 is regret: losing by one point leaves you burning with frustrating regret.
mnemonic.reading: COO, YA, SHE (くやしい) beat you at chess. So frustrating!

examples.ja: 試合に負けて悔しかった。
examples.en: It was so frustrating to lose the match.

items.note: The feeling of losing or being beaten. 残念 is milder disappointment.

mnemonic.meaning: Pull (引) and stretch (張) the rope: you drag it along.
mnemonic.reading: HIP PARR (ひっぱる): you pull so hard your hip pops.

examples.ja: 子供が母親の手を引っ張った。
examples.en: The child tugged at its mother's hand.

items.note: Also "to lead a team": チームを引っ張る.
